questions.stem: A client newly diagnosed with a chronic illness says angrily, “Nobody here listens to me. You all just tell me what to do.” Which nursing response is most therapeutic?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"“That is not accurate; the team has spent considerable time explaining the plan, and we need you to cooperate so treatment can proceed.”","B":"“Try not to be angry with the staff. Everyone is working hard to help you, and focusing on the positive will make this adjustment easier.”","C":"“Why do you think you react this strongly when the team discusses treatment? Understanding the reason may help you accept the plan.”","D":"“It sounds like you feel unheard. Tell me what has been most frustrating about these conversations, and I will listen before responding.”"}}
questions.rationale: The response acknowledges the client's feeling, avoids arguing or premature reassurance, and uses an open-ended invitation to understand the client's concern. This supports therapeutic communication and preserves the client's voice.
questions.source_name: SAMHSA — How to Talk to Someone About Help for Mental Health & Substance Use
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA recommends listening without judgment, showing that you are listening, and using open-ended questions to understand the person's experience.

qc.qc_note: Strict Wave-6 anti-cue rule: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; correct option is neither unique shortest nor unique longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility and wording cues.

questions.stem: During a conversation, a distressed client becomes tearful and silent after describing a recent loss. Which nursing response best demonstrates active, therapeutic listening?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Fill the silence by giving advice about coping strategies so the client does not become more uncomfortable or feel pressured to continue talking.","B":"Remain present, allow the silence, and then use an open-ended or reflective statement that invites the client to continue at their own pace.","C":"Ask a series of specific yes-or-no questions to keep the discussion efficient and prevent the client from becoming overwhelmed by emotion.","D":"Change to a neutral topic until the client stops crying because discussing the loss while visibly distressed can reinforce emotional dependence."}}
questions.rationale: Therapeutic listening includes remaining present, tolerating silence, reflecting what was heard, and using open-ended prompts rather than rushing into advice, interrogation, or topic change.
questions.source_name: SAMHSA — How to Talk to Someone About Help for Mental Health & Substance Use
questions.source_detail: SAMHSA advises listening carefully, allowing supportive conversation, reflecting what the person says, and asking open-ended questions.
